headline: Medium risk: shared networked pair can leak or misroute content, but no direct shared workspace or documented interaction is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or parser bridge is documented between agent_a and agent_b, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, both have broad network egress, and agent_b exposes a REST API surface, so if operator wiring later connects agent_a outputs into agent_b inputs, injection becomes plausible. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or API payloads
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem bridge is introduced
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for reviewed, structured fields
Strip instructions from any text passed from agent_a to agent_b
Use allowlisted JSON schemas for inter-agent handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all bridged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows secrets handled, data classes touched, or a shared workspace, so direct leakage is not documented. Still, agent_a has broad network egress and agent_b calls REST APIs, meaning any future shared content could leave the local boundary. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF either agent is given sensitive files or prompts
IF agent_b REST calls include content originating from agent_a
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or regulated data between the agents
Review outbound destinations for both agents
Use separate service accounts and API keys
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on inter-agent payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show overlapping network egress, but no filesystem, git, db, or OAuth write scopes, and no locking model. That makes direct write conflict unlikely from the documented surfaces. I do not infer hidden write capabilities; uncertainty therefore stays low, not none, because the profiles are sparse.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable resource
IF an orchestrator maps their outputs into a shared state store
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a is a content-writing agent, so its outputs are likely to be consumed as text by agent_b or downstream tooling. Agent_b has a REST API surface and could act on that content without a documented verification step. Because the handoff pathway is plausible in default orchestration but not directly evidenced, medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF no verification or human review is inserted before agent_b acts
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a output
Constrain agent_a to structured, citation-backed outputs
Log and review all agent_a-to-agent_b handoffs
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and neither profile shows secrets or PHI handling. With only docs-only evidence and no compliance mismatch surfaced, a compliance breach pathway is not established. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance-relevant surface is present.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent
IF residency or retention policies diverge for the same data class
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Separate regulated workloads from general content tasks
